title: Encore - How science can help you change your behavior for the better, with Katy Milkman, PhD

sentences.en: Speaking of psychology is taking a summer break, so we're rerunning some of our favorite episodes
sentences.zh: 本期《心理学热线》将暂停播出进行暑期休整，因此我们将重播过去一些最受欢迎的节目

sentences.en: from the paSt. In 2021, I talked to Katie Milkman, a behavioral scientist at the Wharton School of
sentences.zh: 。在2021年，我采访了宾夕法尼亚大学沃顿商学院的行为科学家凯蒂·米尔克曼（Katie Milkman），

sentences.en: the University of Pennsylvania, about how to identify and overcome roadblocks that are getting in the way of making the changes you want to see in your life.
sentences.zh: 探讨了如何识别并克服阻碍你实现生活中预期改变的绊脚石。

sentences.en: I hope you enjoy this episode from the archives.
sentences.zh: 希望你喜欢这期来自档案库的节目。

sentences.en: We'll be back with a new episode next week.
sentences.zh: 我们将在下周推出新节目。

sentences.en: Change is hard.
sentences.zh: 改变是困难的。

sentences.en: When you want to make a change in your life, whether it's eating healthier food, starting an exercise program,
sentences.zh: 当你想要在生活中做出改变时，无论是吃得更健康、开始锻炼计划、

sentences.en: or saving more money, there are many human foibles that can stand in your way.
sentences.zh: 还是存下更多的钱，都有许多人性中的弱点会阻碍你的前进。

sentences.en: Impulsivity, laziness, procrastination, or just plain forgetfulness are among them.
sentences.zh: 冲动、懒惰、拖延，或者单纯的健忘都在其中。

sentences.en: Libraries are full of books offering multi-step plans and other tactics to inspire a new you.
sentences.zh: 图书馆里到处都是提供多步骤计划和其他策略的书籍，旨在激发一个全新的你。

sentences.en: Often, though, these plans fall flat.
sentences.zh: 然而，这些计划往往收效甚微。

sentences.en: Our best intentions aren't enough to overcome the roadblocks of human nature that stand in our way.
sentences.zh: 我们最好的意图并不足以克服阻碍我们前进的人性绊脚石。

sentences.en: But in recent years, psychologists have begun to look at behavior change from a different angle.
sentences.zh: 但近年来，心理学家开始从一个不同的角度来看待行为改变。

sentences.en: Instead of fighting human nature, this research suggests that we should analyze it and then leverage it to work for us rather than against us.
sentences.zh: 这项研究表明，我们不应该与人性对抗，而应该分析它，然后加以利用，让它为我们服务而不是与我们作对。

sentences.en: What does that mean?
sentences.zh: 那意味着什么？

sentences.en: What can we learn from the science of behavior change that can help us make the alterations we want to see in our lives?
sentences.zh: 我们能从行为改变科学中学到什么，来帮助我们做出生活中希望看到的改变？

sentences.en: And how can organizations, companies, and governments use these insights to nudge whole populations into making better choices?
sentences.zh: 组织、公司和政府又该如何利用这些见解来推动整个人群做出更好的选择？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学热线》，这是美国心理学会的旗舰播客，旨在探讨心理学科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯（Kim Mills）。

sentences.en: Our guest today is Dr. Katie Milkman, a professor at the Wharton School of the
sentences.zh: 我们今天的嘉宾是凯蒂·米尔克曼博士，她是沃顿商学院的教授、

sentences.en: University of Pennsylvania and author of the book, How to Change, the Science of Getting from Where You Are to Where You Want to Be.
sentences.zh: 宾夕法尼亚大学学者，也是《如何改变：从现状到理想之境的科学》（How to Change, the Science of Getting from Where You Are to Where You Want to Be）一书的作者。

sentences.en: Her research explores how insights from psychology and economics can be harnessed to change people's behavior for the better on both an individual and a global scale.
sentences.zh: 她的研究探讨了如何利用心理学和经济学的见解，在个人和全球范围内更好地改变人们的行为。

sentences.en: She has explored how relatively simple interventions can help people increase their savings, exercise more, and even get vaccinated, among other things.
sentences.zh: 她曾探讨过相对简单的干预措施如何帮助人们增加储蓄、多做运动甚至接种疫苗等。

sentences.en: She is co-director of the Behavior Change for Good
sentences.zh: 她是沃顿商学院“为了美好而改变”

sentences.en: Initiative at Wharton.
sentences.zh: 计划的联合主任。

sentences.en: She also hosts the Charles Schwab podcast, Choiceology, about the science of
sentences.zh: 她还主持了查尔斯·施瓦布（Charles Schwab）播客《抉择学》（Choiceology），探讨关于

sentences.en: Decision Making.
sentences.zh: 决策的科学。

sentences.en: Dr. Milkman, thank you for joining us today.
sentences.zh: 米尔克曼博士，非常感谢你今天作客我们的节目。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for having me.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢邀请我。

sentences.en: So as I said, your book is entitled How to Change, but in the first chapter, you start with a slightly different premise, which is when to change.
sentences.zh: 正如我所说，你的书名为《如何改变》，但在第一章中，你从一个略有不同的前提开始，那就是何时改变。

sentences.en: You make the point that there are some moments in our lives that are particularly conducive to making change.
sentences.zh: 你指出，在我们生命中的某些时刻特别有利于做出改变。

sentences.en: What has your research found?
sentences.zh: 你的研究发现了什么？

sentences.en: And if you want to make a change in your life, when should you try to do it?
sentences.zh: 如果你想在生活中做出改变，什么时候应该尝试去做？

sentences.en: I love that you opened with this question because it's one of my favorite topics that I've studied.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴你以这个问题开场，因为这是我研究过最喜欢的课题之一。

sentences.en: And actually, it was a question just like the one you asked that that started me on this course.
sentences.zh: 事实上，正是这样一个类似于你提出的问题，让我踏上了这条道路。

sentences.en: I was visiting Google, presenting some of my work on nudges and choice architecture and strategies that could be used by HR managers to
sentences.zh: 当时我正在访问谷歌，展示我关于助推、选择架构以及人力资源经理可用于

sentences.en: help their employees make better decisions and, you know, invest in new skills training,
sentences.zh: 帮助员工做出更好决策、投资新技能培训、

sentences.en: wellness programming, etc.
sentences.zh: 健康计划等的策略的研究。

sentences.en: And I was asked, is there some ideal time to encourage employees to change?
sentences.zh: 有人问我，是否存在鼓励员工改变的理想时机？

sentences.en: And I realized actually there was very little I knew from the academic literature that would help me answer that great question.
sentences.zh: 我意识到，实际上我从学术文献中了解到的、能帮我回答这个好问题的内容少之又少。

sentences.en: So I went back to my research team at the University of Pennsylvania, my former student, Heng Chen Dai, who's now a professor at UCLA's Anderson School,
sentences.zh: 于是我回到了我在宾夕法尼亚大学的研究团队，找了我的前学生、现任加州大学洛杉矶分校安德森商学院教授的戴恒辰（Heng Chen Dai），

sentences.en: and also Jason Reese, who's the head of Behavioral Eyes and a Wharton Senior Fellow.
sentences.zh: 还有行为眼科负责人兼沃顿高级研究员杰森·里恩（Jason Reese）。

sentences.en: We were all really interested in behavior change.
sentences.zh: 我们都对行为改变非常感兴趣。

sentences.en: We started talking about this question and had really strong intuitions right away about when it might make sense to change.
sentences.zh: 我们开始讨论这个问题，并且立刻对什么时候改变才合理有了非常强烈的直觉。

sentences.en: The first thing that came to mind for all of us was that we know people make more resolutions and set more goals around New Year's, right?
sentences.zh: 我们所有人脑海中浮现的第一件事是，我们知道人们在新年时会做出更多决议、设定更多目标，对吧？

sentences.en: So that was that was well established.
sentences.zh: 所以这一点已经得到了充分证实。

sentences.en: We weren't coming up with something wildly new there.
sentences.zh: 我们在那里并没有提出什么极其崭新的东西。

sentences.en: But what we got interested in is whether there was something about that moment that might give us a hint as to other moments in our lives when we might be more open to change.
sentences.zh: 但让我们感兴趣的是，那个时刻是否存在某种特质，可以给我们提供线索，暗示我们生命中的其他时刻可能也对改变更加开放。

sentences.en: And we started reading the literature on autobiographical memory, the way people think about time.
sentences.zh: 于是我们开始阅读关于自传体记忆和人们思考时间方式的文献。

sentences.en: What we learned is that there are moments in our lives that feel like new beginnings.
sentences.zh: 我们了解到，在我们的一生中，有些时刻感觉像是新的开始。

sentences.en: And that's because the way we organize time in our memory is as if our life is a series of chapters.
sentences.zh: 那是因为我们在记忆中组织时间的方式，就好像我们的人生是一系列章节。

sentences.en: And they have sort of beginnings, middles and ends.
sentences.zh: 它们有类似于开始、中间和结尾的部分。

sentences.en: That's how we think about ourselves like characters in a book, instead of thinking about time really truly linearly.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们如何将自己视为书中的角色，而不是真正纯粹线性地去思考时间。

sentences.en: And as a result of that, any moment that feels like a breakpoint can feel like a new beginning to us anytime we're opening a new chapter for any reason.
sentences.zh: 正因如此，任何感觉像分水岭的时刻都让我们觉得像是新的开始，无论何时因为什么原因我们在开启新篇章。

sentences.en: And what happens at New Year's and what we found happens at some other moments as well as we feel like, you know, because we're closing a chapter,
sentences.zh: 新年时会发生什么，以及我们发现其他一些时刻也会发生的情况是，我们会觉得，由于我们在结束一个章节，

sentences.en: we can say that was the old me who didn't manage to quit smoking last year, didn't manage to go to that skills training workshop.
sentences.zh: 我们可以说那是过去的那个我，去年没能戒烟，没能去参加那个技能培训研讨会。

sentences.en: And the new me and the new year, you know, I'm, I'm different, and I can do it.
sentences.zh: 而全新的一年里的那个全新的我，你知道的，我是不同的，我能做到。

sentences.en: So we feel more optimistic.
sentences.zh: 所以我们感觉更加乐观。

sentences.en: And we've found in our research that other moments that systematically feel like new beginnings to us and lead to a similar optimism and tendency to pursue
sentences.zh: 我们在研究中发现，其他那些系统性地让我们感到是新开始并带来类似乐观情绪和追求目标倾向的时刻，

sentences.en: goals include dates like just the start of a new week, the start of a new month, the celebration of
sentences.zh: 包括诸如新一周的开始、新一个月的开始、生日的庆祝、

sentences.en: a birthday, the celebration of certain holidays that we associate with new beginnings.
sentences.zh: 我们与新开始联系在一起的某些节日的庆祝等日期。

sentences.en: So think more Labor Day and less Valentine's Day.
sentences.zh: 所以想想劳动节多于情人节。

sentences.en: And we've, we've shown in our research that people are more likely to do things like visit the gym at these moments, that they're more likely to set goals on a
sentences.zh: 我们在研究中已经表明，人们在这些时刻更有可能做诸如去健身房之类的事情，在这些感觉像新开始的日期里，

sentences.en: popular goal setting website around these, these dates that feel like new beginnings.
sentences.zh: 他们更有可能在一个受欢迎的目标设定网站上设定目标。

sentences.en: And also, if we reach out and say, when would you like to receive reminders to begin pursuing a goal?
sentences.zh: 而且，如果我们伸出援手问：“你什么时候想收到开始追求目标的提醒？”

sentences.en: Or when would you like to start saving, for instance, and we simply label dates differently.
sentences.zh: 或者“你什么时候想开始储蓄？”等等，而我们只是对日期进行了不同的标签化。

sentences.en: If we label a date as an ordinary day, right, no special label, it's not nearly as attractive as if we give it a label that makes it feel like a new beginning.
sentences.zh: 如果我们把一个日期标记为普通的一天，不给它特殊的标签，它的吸引力就远远不如我们给它贴上一个让它感觉像新开始的标签。

sentences.en: So for example, in one study, we labeled March 20th as the first day of spring, in one condition, but not in the other, just it's the third Thursday in March.
sentences.zh: 例如，在一项研究中，我们在一种情况下将3月20日标记为春季的第一天，但在另一种情况下没有，只是说这是3月的第三个星期四。

sentences.en: And we see really huge differences when it's labeled as the first day of spring and how attractive it is as a date to start pursuing a goal, for example.
sentences.zh: 当它被标记为春季的第一天时，我们看到了巨大的差异，比如它作为开始追求目标的日期的吸引力有多大。

sentences.en: So we both see correlationally, sort of naturally, people take advantage of these moments when they're looking at when to change.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们既看到相关性，也就是自然而然地，人们在考虑何时改变时会利用这些时刻。

sentences.en: And we can run experiments and show that if we change the labels associated with certain dates and add fresh start labels, dates that feel like a new beginning, we see this uptick.
sentences.zh: 我们也可以进行实验，表明如果我们改变与某些日期相关的标签，并加入全新开始的标签（即感觉像新开始的日期），我们就会看到这种上升趋势。

sentences.en: So taking that all together, it points to moments that feel like transitions feel like a new beginning of a chapter in our lives,
sentences.zh: 综合所有这些，它指向了那些感觉像转折点、感觉像是我们生活中章节新开始的时刻，

sentences.en: and particularly temporal landmarks that have those features that we've studied include the starts of these calendar cycles.
sentences.zh: 特别是那些具有我们所研究的特征的时间地标，包括这些日历周期的开始。

sentences.en: Okay, but that's an external nudge in a sense.
sentences.zh: 好吧，但从某种意义上说，那是一个外部的助推。

sentences.en: Now, what if I want to make a change, but there isn't some obvious fresh start right now?
sentences.zh: 现在，如果我想做出改变，但眼下并没有某个明显的新开始呢？

sentences.en: Is there something that I can do for myself that would just create a fresh start?
sentences.zh: 有什么我可以为自己做的事情，能够直接创造出一个新的开始吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, it's a wonderful question.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一个极好的问题。

sentences.en: First of all, I would say there are so many dates that even though they are external, you can sort of look for the next one and jump on it, right?
sentences.zh: 首先，我想说的是，有那么多的日期，尽管它们是外部的，你基本上可以寻找下一个并抓住它，对吧？

sentences.en: You know,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，

sentences.en: Monday occurs every seven days, it turns out.
sentences.zh: 周一每七天就会出现一次。

sentences.en: So even though you have to wait around for seven days to
sentences.zh: 所以即使你必须等待七天来……

sentences.en: fairly frequent.
sentences.zh: 相当频繁。

sentences.en: So I do think even with that constraint, they can be useful as moments to sort of lock on to.
sentences.zh: 所以我确实认为，即使有这种限制，它们也可以作为一种可以锁定的时刻发挥作用。

sentences.en: In terms of whether you can create one for yourself, Hengchen, who I mentioned, my former student, she did some work in her dissertation related to a slightly different
sentences.zh: 至于你是否能为自己创造一个，我前面提到过的我的前学生恒辰，她在她的博士论文中做了一些与略微不同

sentences.en: kind of fresh start.
sentences.zh: 那种新开始相关的工作。

sentences.en: She calls it a reset.
sentences.zh: 她称之为重置（reset）。

sentences.en: And it's a different way that it's not a temporal landmark that wipes the slate clean, but rather a change in the way we're tracking our performance that can wipe the slate clean.
sentences.zh: 这是一种不同的方式，它不是一个能擦干净石板的时间地标，而是一种改变我们追踪表现方式的改变，从而可以擦净石板重新开始。

sentences.en: So for instance, I wear a Fitbit and every morning I sort of feel like I have a bit of a fresh start because yesterday I had accumulated, you know, maybe a
sentences.zh: 例如，我戴着Fitbit，每天早晨我都会觉得有点像是重新开始，因为昨天我积累的步数，你知道，可能是一个

sentences.en: pathetically low number of steps, maybe a really high number of steps.
sentences.zh: 可怜的低步数，也可能是一个非常高的步数。

sentences.en: Either way, I wake up and it says zero again.
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，我醒来时它又显示为零了。

sentences.en: And that's a reset and a fresh start in a sense.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，这是一个重置和一个新的开始。

sentences.en: There's all these different ways in which we track our performance, whether it's sales performance, if you're in an organization,
sentences.zh: 我们追踪表现的方式有各种各样不同的形式，无论是销售业绩，如果你在一个组织中，

sentences.en: whether you're a professional athlete and you're sort of tracking your stats for the season
sentences.zh: 无论你是一名职业运动员，并且你在追踪这个赛季的统计数据，

sentences.en: and things get reset at different frequencies, grades for students, whether it's semester, quarter.
sentences.zh: 而且各种数据会以不同的频率重置，学生的成绩也是如此，无论是按学期还是按季度。

sentences.en: So one thing that we may have some more control over, especially if we're tracking ourselves, is when these resets occur.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们可以拥有更多控制权的一件事，特别是在我们追踪自己的时候，就是这些重置发生的时间。

sentences.en: And if we're having a rough time, it turns out resets can be really valuable as a motivator to improve and set goals and do better.
sentences.zh: 如果我们正经历一段艰难时期，事实证明重置可以作为一种非常宝贵的动力，用来改善自我、设定目标和做得更好。

sentences.en: Interestingly, her research also finds that resets are harmful.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，她的研究还发现重置也会带来危害。

sentences.en: And I think this is very intuitive, actually, in cases where we're doing really well.
sentences.zh: 我认为这实际上非常直观，在我们做得很好的情况下。

sentences.en: So you want to wipe the slate clean and have a fresh start when things aren't going your way, when you need the motivation to do something you haven't managed to do.
sentences.zh: 因此，当事情不顺心时，当你需要动力去做一些你一直没能做到的事情时，你会想要擦净石板重新开始拥有一个新的开端。

sentences.en: But when you're on a roll, it's actually disruptive and harmful to have a fresh start.
sentences.zh: 但当你顺风顺水、势头正劲时，重新开始实际上具有破坏性和负面影响。

sentences.en: So we do have to use this particular tool with some caution.
sentences.zh: 所以我们确实必须谨慎使用这个特定的工具。

sentences.en: You started out as an engineering student and you write in the book that in some ways you approach behavior change as an engineering problem.
sentences.zh: 你最初是一名工程系学生，你在书中写道，你在某种程度上将行为改变视为一个工程问题。

sentences.en: What do you mean by that?
sentences.zh: 你这话是什么意思？

sentences.en: Yeah, it's funny to be on this podcast and I'm often labeled a psychologiSt. You will laugh.
sentences.zh: 是的，在这个播客上听到这个很有趣，而且我经常被贴上心理学家的标签。你会笑的。

sentences.en: I have literally never taken a psychology class in my entire life.
sentences.zh: 我这一辈子实际上从来没有上过一节心理学课。

sentences.en: My undergraduate degree and PhD are both in engineering.
sentences.zh: 我的本科和博士学位都是工程学。

sentences.en: And so it's a different way of looking at the world.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一种看待世界的天壤之别的方式。

sentences.en: It's sort of looking for problems that you can solve by pulling the right pieces together in order to plug a hole or fix a gap or improve a structure.
sentences.zh: 它有点像是在寻找可以通过将正确的拼图拼凑在一起以堵住漏洞、修复差距或改善结构来解决的问题。

sentences.en: That is the way that I was trained to think.
sentences.zh: 这就是我受到的思维训练方式。

sentences.en: And it turns out, I think it's quite a useful way of looking at a lot of psychology problems, especially in my field of
sentences.zh: 事实证明，我认为这是看待许多心理学问题的一种非常有用的大脑视角，尤其是在我的领域——

sentences.en: behavioral science, where we have spent a lot of time documenting errors and judgment, the ways that people make systematic mistakes.
sentences.zh: 行为科学中，我们花了大量时间来记录判断上的错误，即人们犯下系统性错误的方式。

sentences.en: But if you want to actually start correcting some of those mistakes, having this engineering mindset, like, you know, what, how can I build a structure that plugs that hole?
sentences.zh: 但如果你真的想开始纠正其中一些错误，拥有这种工程思维，比如，你知道的，我如何建立一个结构来堵住那个漏洞？

sentences.en: How can I fill that gap is a really useful perspective, I think.
sentences.zh: 我如何填补那个空白？我认为这是一个非常实用的视角。

sentences.en: And I've tried to bring that to my work.
sentences.zh: 我一直在试图将这一点带入我的工作中。

sentences.en: I've always been solutions oriented and looking for ways that what we know about the human

sentences.en: So some of your first research on behavior change was what you call temptation bundling,

sentences.zh: 你能给我们讲讲这个故事，并解释什么是诱惑捆绑，以及它如何帮助人们改变行为吗？

sentences.en: I think another psychologist named Carrie Morwidge is the person who taught me that term.
sentences.zh: 我想另一位名叫卡丽·莫威奇（Carrie Morwidge）的心理学家是教给我这个词的人。

sentences.en: I love, I love that term.
sentences.zh: 我很喜欢、我很喜欢这个词。

sentences.en: It's what drew me into the field, honestly, was that I was doing some me search.
sentences.zh: 坦白说，正是自我研究吸引我进入了这个领域。

sentences.en: So I was a graduate student at the time in engineering and struggling with tough classes and tired at the end of a long day.
sentences.zh: 所以当时我是一名工程学的研究生，正在与艰难的课程作斗争，在漫长的一天结束时感到筋疲力尽。

sentences.en: And all I wanted to do when I came home and should have been working on problem sets was curl up on my couch with, you
sentences.zh: 当我回到家、本该去做习题集时，我唯一的愿望就是蜷缩在沙发上，

sentences.en: know, entertainment, a juicy page turner or binge watch Netflix, one of the above.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，享受娱乐，看一本让人爱不释手的书或者疯狂刷Netflix，二者居其一。

sentences.en: I was struggling to find the motivation to get my work done.
sentences.zh: 我一直在努力寻找动力来完成我的工作。

sentences.en: Similarly, I knew that I really needed to exercise regularly.
sentences.zh: 同样，我知道我真的需要定期锻炼。

sentences.zh: 这对我的身体和心理健康都很重要。

sentences.zh: 我是一名终身运动员，但我就是无法把自己拖到健身房去。

sentences.en: And especially at the end of those long days when I was feeling worn out, I sort of had this epiphany, a little me search.
sentences.zh: 特别是在那些漫长一天的结束、我感到精疲力竭的时候，我有点顿悟了，这是一次小小的自我研究。

sentences.en: And by the way, many other people have had this epiphany independently, which was what if I only let myself enjoy these indulgent entertainment sources while
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，许多其他人也独立地有了这种顿悟，那就是：如果我只允许自己在

sentences.en: I'm exercising?
sentences.zh: 锻炼的同时享受这些纵情声色的娱乐来源呢？

sentences.en: Maybe that would actually drag me to the gym.
sentences.zh: 也许这实际上会把我拖到健身房去。

sentences.en: And so, and maybe also I'd stop wasting time at home, binge watching TV when I should have been doing my problem sets.
sentences.zh: 所以，也许我也不会把时间浪费在家里疯狂看电视上，而本该去做我的习题集。

sentences.en: So I tried this out.
sentences.zh: 于是我尝试了这个方法。

sentences.en: I made a new rule that I was only allowed to indulge in entertainment while I was exercising.
sentences.zh: 我制定了一条新规则：只有在锻炼时，我才可以放纵自己享受娱乐。

sentences.en: And it was life altering.
sentences.zh: 这改变了我的人生。

sentences.en: All of a sudden I'd come home from a long day and all I wanted to do was rush to the gym to find out what happened.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，我结束了漫长的一天回到家，我唯一的愿望就是冲向健身房，去看看接下来发生了什么。

sentences.en: And the latest, I was actually, I got into audio books, lowbrow audio books, like, um, well, this isn't very lowbrow, Harry Potter, James Patterson, you know, the hunger
sentences.zh: 最近，实际上，我迷上了有声书，那些通俗的有声书，比如，嗯，这其实不算太通俗，哈利·波特、詹姆斯·帕特森，你知道的，饥饿

sentences.en: games, page turners, thrillers.
sentences.zh: 游戏、扣人心弦的书籍、惊悚小说。

sentences.en: I would, I would want to know what happened next to these characters.
sentences.zh: 我会、我会想知道这些角色接下来发生了什么。

sentences.en: So I dash off to the gym.
sentences.zh: 所以我冲向健身房。

sentences.en: I get in these great workouts where I didn't even notice that I was exercising because I was flying so faSt. Normally exercise was a drag, but I was so
sentences.zh: 我在那里进行了很棒的锻炼，甚至都没有注意到自己在锻炼，因为我过得太快了。通常锻炼是一种折磨，但我太

sentences.en: into these characters and the stories I kept going.
sentences.zh: 沉迷于这些角色和故事了，于是我坚持了下去。

sentences.en: And then I'd come home and I was totally refreshed and rejuvenated, ready to get my work done.
sentences.zh: 然后我回到家，整个人完全神清气爽、恢复了活力，准备好完成我的工作了。

sentences.en: And there's no distractions.
sentences.zh: 而且没有任何干扰。

sentences.en: And I thought, wow, this is really working for me.
sentences.zh: 我想，哇，这对我真的很有用。

sentences.en: And I should see if this could help other people.
sentences.zh: 我应该看看这是否能帮助其他人。

sentences.en: So I ended up doing some experiments to test whether or not what I now call temptation bundling or linking something that
sentences.zh: 所以我最后做了一些实验，来测试我称之为“诱惑捆绑”的机制是否有效，也就是将一个

sentences.en: you find a pleasure and a temptation with an activity that would otherwise feel like a chore in order to make it more, you know, endurable, more, more pleasant could help people.
sentences.zh: 你觉得是一种享受和诱惑的活动，与一个本来感觉像是苦差事的活动结合起来，使其变得更，你知道的，更容易忍受、更令人愉快，从而看看能否帮助到人们。

sentences.en: So we've run a couple of experiments now showing that temptation bundling can be a helpful tool, uh, to other people, not just me, not an N of one.
sentences.zh: 所以我们现在已经做了几个实验，表明诱惑捆绑可以是一个有用的工具，呃，对其他人来说，不仅仅是我，样本不只是我一个人。

sentences.en: So one experiment, the first one we did, we randomly assigned people to a group where
sentences.zh: 所以第一个实验，我们做的第一个实验，是随机把人们分到一个组里，

sentences.en: they would, uh, be given tempting audio novels that they could load onto iPods and then listen to the first 30 minutes while they were doing a workout at the gym.
sentences.zh: 在这个组里，呃，他们会得到有吸引力的有声小说，可以下载到iPod里，然后在健身房锻炼的前30分钟听。

sentences.en: And we told them if they wanted to hear what happened next and whichever tempting novel they'd picked from a menu of 80, we gave them that had been pretested.
sentences.zh: 我们告诉他们，如果想知道接下来发生什么，在从我们提供的80本经过预先测试的有声小说菜单中选出的任何一本中，

sentences.en: Well, they would have to come back to the gym because we'd be holding their iPod hostage in a locked monitored locker.
sentences.zh: 好吧，他们必须回到健身房，因为我们会把他们的iPod锁在一个有监控的储物柜里扣押起来。

sentences.en: They could only access when they came in for a workout.
sentences.zh: 只有当他们进来锻炼时才能使用。

sentences.en: And we compared that group's exercise habits to a control group that also did a 30 minute workout at the start.
sentences.zh: 我们将这一组的锻炼习惯与一个对照组进行了比较，对照组在开始时也进行了30分钟的锻炼。

sentences.en: Also owned iPods was also given an equally valued, um, gift, a gift certificate to Barnes and
sentences.zh: 同样拥有iPod，也得到了等值的礼物，一份巴诺书店的

sentences.en: Noble, which they could of course use to buy audio books if they wanted, but we gave them no suggestion to temptation bundle.
sentences.zh: 礼品卡，他们当然可以用它来买有声书（如果他们愿意的话），但我们没有向他们建议进行诱惑捆绑。

sentences.en: And what we found is that temptation bundling did increase exercise pretty substantially in the short term.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，诱惑捆绑确实在短期内相当显著地增加了锻炼量。

sentences.en: So the study went for 10 weeks.
sentences.zh: 所以这项研究持续了10周。

sentences.en: The effects were robust for seven weeks.
sentences.zh: 这种效果在七周内都很稳定。

sentences.en: Then along came Thanksgiving break.
sentences.zh: 然后感恩节假期就来了。

sentences.en: We did this at a university gym, the gym closed,
sentences.zh: 我们在大学健身房做的实验，健身房关门了，

sentences.en: everybody went home.
sentences.zh: 大家都回家了。

sentences.en: And, and this was actually, I think another interesting part of the research, the effect was totally wiped out by that period of forced separation from the tempting stimulus.
sentences.zh: 而这实际上，我认为是研究中另一个有趣的部分，由于那段被迫与诱惑刺激分离的时期，这种效果被完全抹杀了。

sentences.en: So, uh, you know, we, we've done subsequent studies where we show it can have a more durable effect
sentences.zh: 所以，呃，你知道的，我们做过后续研究，表明它可以产生更持久的效果，

sentences.en: when you don't have that kind of disruption, but it also links back to what we were talking about with
sentences.zh: 当你没有那种中断的时候，但这也回到了我们之前讨论过的关于

sentences.en: fresh starts and how resets and disruption can be good in some cases, but when you're on a roll can be harmful.
sentences.zh: “全新开始”的话题，以及重置和中断在某些情况下可能是好的，但当你顺风顺水时则可能是有害的。

sentences.en: You get kind of dependent then on your iPod in order to go to the gym.
sentences.zh: 你会变得有点依赖你的iPod才能去健身房。

sentences.en: If you don't have it, when you go back home, forget it, I'm done.
sentences.zh: 如果你没有它，当你回到家时，算了吧，我不练了。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: It'd break.
sentences.zh: 这就中断了。

sentences.en: And there's anyway, all of these things, I think part of what makes them so interesting is there's, there are a few
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，所有这些事情，我认为它们之所以如此引人入胜，部分原因在于有那么几件事情

sentences.en: things that are just sort of, um, totally unambiguous, always work.
sentences.zh: 并不是那种完全明确、永远管用的东西。

sentences.en: There's no moderators.
sentences.zh: 没有什么调节变量。

sentences.en: And that's one of the things that's so interesting about studying humans is that there's always interesting complexity to unpack anyway.
sentences.zh: 这也是研究人类如此有趣的地方之一，因为总是有有趣的复杂性需要去剖析，无论如何。

sentences.en: So that's, that's the work on temptation bundling.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是关于诱惑捆绑的研究。

sentences.en: And I've talked about it only in the context of exercise, but just want to point out for listeners who have other kinds of
sentences.zh: 我一直在锻炼的语境下谈论它，但我想向听众指出，对于那些有其他类型、

sentences.en: behaviors that they find to be chores or burdens, and they're trying to engage in more.
sentences.zh: 觉得是苦差事或负担的行为，并且正试图做更多这些行为的人来说。

sentences.en: It's a tool that theoretically should be applicable to lots of settings in life, not just getting yourself to the gym.
sentences.zh: 从理论上讲，这是一个适用于生活中许多场景的工具，不仅仅是促使你去健身房。

sentences.en: So you can think about, you know, only letting yourself listen to your favorite podcast, say this one while you're doing household chores or cooking fresh meals.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以考虑，比方说，只允许自己在做家务或烹饪新鲜饭菜时听最喜欢的播客，比如这个播客。

sentences.en: If those are goals that you want to fulfill or only letting yourself pick up a favorite treat or snack on the way to hit the books
sentences.zh: 如果这些是你想实现的目标，或者只允许自己在去图书馆啃书本的路上，

sentences.en: at the library, if that feels like a chore, but you want something to make it more of a pleasure.
sentences.zh: 顺便买一个最喜欢的点心或零食，如果这感觉像个苦差事，但你需要点东西让它更有趣的话。

sentences.en: So there's lots of ways we can create temptation bundles beyond exercise, but that is where I first did it and studied it.
sentences.zh: 所以除了锻炼之外，我们还有很多方法可以创造诱惑捆绑，但那是我最初做实验和研究它的地方。

sentences.en: So your book is organized into chapters, each covering a different aspect of human nature, a couple of which I mentioned in the introduction, impulsivity, laziness,
sentences.zh: 所以你的书是按章节组织的，每一章涵盖人性的不同方面，我在引言中提到过其中的几个，冲动、懒惰、

sentences.en: procrastination.
sentences.zh: 拖延。

sentences.en: Can you talk about your favorite examples from the book about how we can work with, rather than against these traits when we're trying to make change?
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈书中你最喜欢的例子吗，关于在我们试图做出改变时，如何顺应而不是对抗这些特质？

sentences.en: Yeah, probably my favorite example is one that is, it's really well known, and yet it's so important.
sentences.zh: 对，我最喜欢的例子可能是一个非常著名，却又极其重要的例子。

sentences.en: So I'm just going to harp on it anyway.
sentences.zh: 所以我还是要喋喋不休地讲它。

sentences.en: I think it's the power of defaults.
sentences.zh: 我认为这就是默认值的力量。

sentences.en: And I think this is one of the biggest wins from behavioral science, and it has to do with laziness.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是行为科学取得的最大胜利之一，它与懒惰有关。

sentences.en: So in general, we humans prefer to take the path of least resistance, whatever the easiest route is to, you know, collecting my
sentences.zh: 所以总的来说，我们人类更喜欢走阻力最小的路线，无论最简单的途径是什么，比如领取我的

sentences.en: paycheck or getting my lunch or, you know, whatever it is, whatever goal you have, we're always looking for the shortcuts in the easiest way instead of the hardest work path.
sentences.zh: 薪水，或者买午餐，或者无论是什么，无论你有什么目标，我们总是在寻找捷径和最简单的办法，而不是最艰难的工作路线。

sentences.en: And that actually, of course, is a challenge, right?
sentences.zh: 当然，这实际上是一个挑战，对吧？

sentences.en: When it comes to trying to get yourself in great physical shape or, you know, earning your PhD, the fact that we're looking for shortcuts does not really help, right?
sentences.zh: 当你想让自己保持极佳的体形，或者，你知道的，获得博士学位时，我们寻找捷径的心态其实并没有什么帮助，对吧？

sentences.en: It's often a barrier to change.
sentences.zh: 这通常是改变的障碍。

sentences.en: And so I talk a lot about that in the book.
sentences.zh: 我在书中对此进行了很多讨论。

sentences.en: But one of the things that's so interesting is that defaults flip this on its head and turn laziness into an asset.
sentences.zh: 但非常有趣的一点是，默认值彻底扭转了这一局面，把懒惰变成了一种资产。

sentences.en: So a default is the sort of option you will end up with in a situation if you literally don't lift a finger, if you do nothing.
sentences.zh: 所以，默认值就是如果你字面上什么都不做、不费吹灰之力，最终在某种情况下会得到的选项。

sentences.en: So your computer comes with default settings, right?
sentences.zh: 所以你的电脑自带默认设置，对吧？

sentences.en: You turn it on, it has some background screen, it has default fonts, it probably has a default browser, there's all these things that are just there.
sentences.zh: 你打开它，它有一些背景屏幕，它有默认字体，它可能有一个默认浏览器，所有这些东西都是现成的。

sentences.en: And if you take the path of least resistance,
sentences.zh: 如果你走阻力最小的路线，

sentences.en: well, that's what you end up with.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这就是你最终得到的。

sentences.en: And so I think one of the really interesting things is, once you start to recognize their power, and they've been studied in so many different contexts,
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得非常有趣的一点是，一旦你开始认识到它们的力量——它们已经在这么多不同的语境中被研究过了——

sentences.en: it's actually not something I've studied, but lots of wonderful scholars in this association have,
sentences.zh: 这其实不是我研究过的东西，但这个协会里有很多出色的学者研究过，

sentences.en: I'll just mention, for instance, Eric Johnson and Dan Goldstein have some wonderful work on how much default organ donation policies change our decisions.
sentences.zh: 我只想举个例子，比如埃里克·约翰逊（Eric Johnson）和丹·戈德斯坦（Dan Goldstein）有一些非常精彩的研究，关于默认的器官捐赠政策能在多大程度上改变我们的决定。

sentences.en: So countries where you're defaulted into being an organ donor, but you can just opt out trivially easily by sort of checking a box and
sentences.zh: 因此，那些默认你成为器官捐赠者，但你可以通过勾选一个方框和

sentences.en: signing your name on a basic form, have vastly higher rates of organ donorship than countries where you have to, I said it the wrong way.
sentences.zh: 在基本表格上签名来极其轻松地退出的国家，其器官捐赠率远高于那些你必须——我刚才说反了。

sentences.en: No, I said it the right way, where you have to opt in, which is what we have in the United States.
sentences.zh: 不，我说对了，是你必须选择加入的国家，也就是我们在美国的做法。

sentences.en: So in the United States, you go to the DMV, you check a box, you opt in, it's trivially easy, but we have lower donation rates because I had to take some action.
sentences.zh: 所以在美国，你去车管所（DMV），勾选一个方框，你选择加入，这极其简单，但我们的捐赠率较低，因为我必须采取某种行动。

sentences.en: And we always look for the path of least resistance.
sentences.zh: 而且我们总是寻找阻力最小的路线。

sentences.en: So anyway, this is a organ donation is a particularly tricky one, because it's more than just whether you
sentences.zh: 所以无论如何，器官捐赠是一个特别棘手的问题，因为这不仅仅关乎你

sentences.en: sign your name and check a box and are opted in or opted out that determines what actually happens with organs.
sentences.zh: 是否签名、勾选方框并选择加入或退出，来决定器官最终如何处理。

sentences.en: But it shows the power because of these huge differences of a default policy, and how important it is to put deep thought into that if you want to change behavior in a positive
sentences.zh: 但它展示了力量，因为默认政策会带来巨大的差异，如果你想朝着积极的方向改变行为，深入思考这一点是多么重要。

sentences.en: direction.
sentences.zh: 方向。

sentences.zh: 所以当我们有旨在帮助人们实现目标的默认设置时，

sentences.en: right, we default them into getting apple slices with their meal instead of French fries on the side.
sentences.zh: 对吧，我们默认让他们吃饭时配苹果片，而不是作为配菜的炸薯条。

sentences.en: Or we default people into say being organ donors, although again, that one, that one has some complexity.
sentences.zh: 或者我们默认人们成为器官捐赠者，尽管再次说明，那一个，那一个有些复杂。

sentences.zh: 所有这些选择，它们利用了懒惰来帮助我们实现目标。

sentences.zh: 例如，我浏览器的首页不是Facebook或Twitter。

sentences.en: It's the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 是《纽约时报》。

sentences.en: So every day I encounter some news when I open it up, and I don't get sucked into a vortex of something that maybe I'm going to be tempted to waste time with.
sentences.zh: 所以每天我打开它时都会看到一些新闻，而不会被卷入某个我可能会经受诱惑去浪费时间的漩涡中。

sentences.en: Instead, I'm getting something that I consider enriching.
sentences.zh: 相反，我得到的是我认为有营养的内容。

sentences.zh: 尽管我给你的回答是我完全赞同的，你知道的，我非常坚信答案就是我们继续使用这些工具。

sentences.en: I still study often tactics that an employer or a school or, you know, um, a gym,
sentences.zh: 但我仍然经常研究雇主、学校或者，你知道的，嗯，健身房，

sentences.en: you know, an organization that's trying to help people create positive lasting change can wrap around beneficiaries to help them achieve that durably.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，一个试图帮助人们创造积极持久改变的组织，可以为受益者提供哪些支持，以帮助他们持久地实现这一目标。

sentences.en: And, um, so I'm looking into like, what are the tools that those kinds of organizations can offer to their employees, their members, their students
sentences.zh: 所以，嗯，我在研究诸如这类组织可以向其员工、会员、学生提供什么工具

sentences.en: that will carry them forward for as long as possible?
sentences.zh: 能够让他们尽可能长时间地坚持下去？

sentences.en: Um, and, and what are, what are the kinds of features of programming that make it the most effective?
sentences.zh: 嗯，而且，什么样的节目特色能让它最有效？

sentences.en: You know, is it mindset?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，是心态吗？

sentences.en: Is it social?
sentences.zh: 是社交吗？

sentences.en: Are there other tactics we haven't studied yet that do create more lasting change?
sentences.zh: 还有其他我们尚未研究过、确实能创造更持久改变的策略吗？

sentences.en: So I'm really eager to, to explore that.
sentences.zh: 所以我真的很渴望去探索这一点。

sentences.en: I'm also really interested in understanding better when people have goal failure, how they stand up again, you know, fresh starts are part of it, of course.
sentences.zh: 我也非常想更好地理解，当人们遭遇目标失败时，他们是如何重新振作起来的，当然，重新开始是其中的一部分。

sentences.en: And there's other tactics in the book too, but I think recovering from failure is under, it's so important because we
sentences.zh: 书中还有其他策略，但我认为从失败中恢复过来是被低估的，它是如此重要，因为当我们

sentences.en: almost always fail when we set out to achieve a goal, at least once we have to get back up again, if we're going to get to our final destination.
sentences.zh: 着手实现一个目标时，几乎总是会失败，如果我们想到达最终的目的地，至少有一次我们必须重新站起来。

sentences.en: And I think there's a lot more to know about how to do that.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为关于如何做到这一点，还有很多需要了解的地方。
